meta.title: Ch 5: Security Valuation — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 5 (Security Valuation).

questions.q: The Hamada extension is irrelevant to a dividend-discount critique because the H-D model assumes:
o: Payout ratio constant with growth g; value is INDEPENDENT of the policy when ROR > k (dividend irrelevance)
questions.why: H-D shows value unchanged under alternative payout choices given investment policy — irrelevance rests on perfect capital markets and ROR>k; Gordon fixes payout and growth, a different animal.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the two models are always paired as options AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Gordon: grow like the payout. H-D: pick any payout — the pie bakes the same.

questions.q: Free cash flow to equity (FCFE) differs from FCFF mainly by:
o: Subtracting interest expense after tax and net borrowings
questions.why: FCFF is pre-debt; FCFE = FCFF − interest(1−t) + net new borrowings (repayments deducted).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the bridge between the two flows is exact MCQ material AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: FCFF pays the whole table; FCFE leaves the diner (debt) its bill and its wallet.

questions.q: CB with face Rs 100, conversion ratio 8, market price Rs 14: conversion value:
questions.why: Conversion value = ratio × share price = 8×14 = Rs 112 vs straight value 100 ⇒ convertible floor is the higher, plus option premium.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the floor concept with quick multiplication AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The bond sleeps under the shares' floor: never below max(straight, conversion).

questions.q: FCFF for a year: EBIT Rs 200 crore, tax 30%, depreciation Rs 40 crore, capital expenditure Rs 90 crore, increase in working capital Rs 20 crore. FCFF is:
questions.why: NOPAT = 200 × 0.7 = 140; + depreciation 40 − capex 90 − ΔWC 20 = Rs 70 crore. Adding back depreciation then deducting it again (110) or forgetting capex entirely are the traps.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the FCFF recipe order is the valuation arithmetic exam Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Taxes first, then cash: EBIT(1−t) + depreciation − capex − working-capital creep.

questions.q: The bird-in-the-hand argument says:
o: Dividends are certain so payout raises value
Growth firms should pay out fully
questions.why: B-I-H (Gordon/Lintner): certain dividends discounted at lower risk-adjusted rate than uncertain capital gains — value rises with payout (the MM rebuttal is the exam's other half).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the assumption-vs-MM contrast Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A rupee paid today shrugs at future ambiguity; MM calls that a taste, not a discount.

questions.q: Under MM dividend irrelevance (perfect markets), an investor wanting cash NOW when the firm pays none should:
o: Pay a special dividend from reserves
Sell a slice of shares — same consumption, no wealth loss
questions.why: Homemade dividends = float the slice; share price ex-dividend reflects the cut; consumption pattern identical; transaction costs are the imperfection to note.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the homemade-dividend argument names the irrelevance proof Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Homemade dividends: sell shares to create cash flows; value of firm unchanged.

questions.q: A convertible bond's straight value Rs 98 and conversion value Rs 112. The price floor argument says it should not trade below:
o: At least Rs 112 — conversion value governs now
Zero time value if in money
questions.why: The floor is the HIGHER of the two: investors can convert for 112 ⇒ below that arbitrage; the optionality can add above the max.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — floor = higher-of is the definitional convertible line AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Value = max(straight, conversion) + option premium considerations.
